calibration_rules.family_failure: FAIL if complete-family FWER Wilson lower bound exceeds .075; no FWER estimate/interval if any panel was incomplete.
calibration_rules.marginal_failure: FAIL if any marginal Wilson lower bound exceeds .075; otherwise report all rates and intervals as synthetic diagnostics.
calibration_rules.monte_carlo_intervals: Two-sided 95% Wilson intervals for each marginal available-cell Bernoulli rejection rate and for complete-family any-rejection rate. Marginal intervals are pointwise, not simultaneous.
calibration_rules.overall: FAIL if any marginal or estimable family lower bound exceeds .075; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE if any family is refused, precision floor is unmet, any upper bound exceeds .075, runtime fails, or assumptions are not validated. No post hoc relaxation.
calibration_rules.pass: Only if every scenario has zero refused families, at least 2000 independent panels, all marginal and family Wilson upper bounds <=.075, and all declared assumptions are defensible. Otherwise INCONCLUSIVE; passing synthetic calibration would not itself validate markets.
calibration_rules.power_non_vacuity: No positive-effect power run is planned: under 28 days, sparse cells, a four-lag HAC variance and the extreme first Holm threshold, null size calibration is the necessary gate, not evidence of useful discovery power. This diagnostic cannot establish that the method has adequate power; no efficacy claim is allowed.
calibration_rules.precision: 2000 independent panels/scenario is the minimum predeclared FWER precision floor. Planned 1000/scenario is deliberately below this floor; a PASS is impossible under this single bounded run.
calibration_rules.replication_unit: One complete independently generated 28x132 daily sum/count panel per replicate; correlated hypotheses do not increase Monte Carlo sample size.
calibration_rules.runtime_failure: A 90-second internal monotonic deadline, SIGTERM, exception or artifact >8 MiB saves RUNTIME_OR_EXECUTION_FAILURE with partial diagnostics and nonzero status. Do not retry, tune, change seeds, or increase/decrease replicates after seeing results.

config.event_counts: On an active cell-day, 2 + Bernoulli(0.5) events; counts are independent of outcomes.
config.tail: One-sided upper-tail Student t reference with 27 degrees of freedom; finite analytic values are not Monte Carlo-ranked.

design.daily_panel: Exactly 28 UTC calendar rows and 132 fixed hypothesis columns. S is the sum of event outcomes for a cell-day; C is its event count. Empty days have S=0,C=0 and remain in the calendar.
design.estimand: For each fixed cell, the event-weighted mean theta = sum_d S[d]/sum_d C[d], under the one-sided null theta <= 0.
explicit_assumptions: The daily influence process is approximately stationary over the fold, has finite fourth moments and summable weak dependence.
The Bartlett lag-4 truncation captures enough dependence for the HAC standard error; dependence beyond four days is not modeled.
The Student-t approximation is adequate with only 28 calendar days; this is a strong, unverified small-sample assumption.
Event counts and missingness are exogenous to outcomes, or inference is interpreted conditional on the realized counts/mask. Outcome-dependent event activity is not covered.
The synthetic calibration generators span the relevant failure modes. Finite calibration cannot establish these assumptions for real market outcomes.
Holm controls FWER under arbitrary cross-hypothesis dependence only when each marginal p-value is super-uniform. The proposed HAC/t p-values have no finite-sample super-uniformity guarantee.
design.multiplicity: Holm step-down at alpha .05 over exactly all 132 finite cell p-values. If any hypothesis is invalid, the entire family is refused; no dropping invalid cells or changing family size.
design.null_and_calibration_target: All 132 event-weighted cell means are zero in synthetic null panels. Assess marginal size at .05 and complete-family Holm FWER across independently generated whole panels.
design.small_sample_reference: One-sided Student-t tail with df=27. The reference distribution is an asymptotic small-sample approximation, not an exact result for a 28-day dependent panel.
design.statistic: For each cell, form X[d]=S[d]-theta_hat*C[d]. Estimate long-run variance of sum_d X[d] by Bartlett HAC: gamma0 + 2*sum_{l=1..4}(1-l/5)*gamma_l, with gamma_l=sum_{d=l..27}X[d]*X[d-l]. Studentize theta_hat by sqrt(HAC)/sum C.
design.unknown_dependence_estimator: A fixed, no-tuning Newey-West/Bartlett lag-4 long-run variance estimator on calendar-day influence values. It allows arbitrary within-day covariance and estimates serial covariance only through four lags.
design.why_not_authorized: This candidate is an auditable practical estimator, not an oracle replacement or proven valid inference method. It can only be considered further if the preregistered calibration passes; empirical failure, insufficient precision, or unmet assumptions leaves criterion 4 unsatisfied.

missing_and_sparse_rules.cell_eligibility: Require at least 30 observed events and at least 10 nonempty UTC dates for each hypothesis.
missing_and_sparse_rules.empty_hypothesis: A zero-event cell has no statistic and no p-value. Any such cell refuses the complete 132-family Holm test.
missing_and_sparse_rules.invalid_input: Refuse a cell/family for nonfinite sums, noninteger/negative counts, nonzero sum with zero count, nonrectangular panels, or calendar length other than 28.
missing_and_sparse_rules.partial_results: Marginal rates may be reported only as explicitly conditional available-cell diagnostics with valid-replicate denominators. If any replicate refuses any family cell, no unconditional FWER estimate or interval is reported for that scenario.

p_value_resolution.resolution_note: The deterministic Student-t CDF can numerically resolve the first Holm threshold; this says nothing about Monte Carlo calibration precision.

synthetic_cases.name: iid_heteroskedastic
synthetic_cases.null: Independent Gaussian event errors with per-day shared lognormal volatility; varying event counts and zero-activity days.
synthetic_cases.role: Independent-day heteroskedastic marginal-size and Holm baseline.

synthetic_cases.name: serial_heteroskedastic
synthetic_cases.null: Zero-mean AR(1) common and arm factors (rho=.65/.45) plus event noise, with time-varying volatility and counts.

synthetic_cases.name: shared_cross_cell_heteroskedastic
synthetic_cases.null: Strong shared global and arm Gaussian factors, day-varying volatility and event noise; full 132-cell panels generated together.
synthetic_cases.role: Cross-cell dependence, heteroskedasticity and dependence-aware whole-family Holm calibration.

synthetic_cases.name: sparse_and_empty_cells
synthetic_cases.null: Sparse day/cell event masks with at least some cells forced to have no events in a replicate; outcomes remain zero-mean and heteroskedastic.
synthetic_cases.role: Evaluate sparse conditional marginals and fail-closed invalid complete-family behavior; unconditional FWER is not estimable when any replicate is refused.
